reasons.reason: Most requirements are grounded, but R3 and R3-MAP require documenting that vehicle_reference links casualty to vehicle. The cited facts only show a vehicle_reference column in the vehicle and casualty headers and a collision_index join note; no cited source fact explicitly states the casualty-to-vehicle linkage via vehicle_reference. That part is therefore unsupported in the evidence graph.

All eight requirements are linked to at least one rubric item, but R2-REQS imports R8's summing/not-averaging rule into R2, creating overlapping scoring, and its full-credit text does not explicitly enumerate all R2 variables such as collision_year, the two injury_based flags, vehicle_reference, and casualty_reference. This weakens alignment between R2 and its rubric.

R3-MAP's full-credit requires an unsupported vehicle_reference casualty-to-vehicle join claim; the cited evidence only establishes field presence and the collision_index join. R2-REQS also double-counts the R8 summing/not-averaging rule and does not explicitly test all R2 variables. The R1-FILE existence check is acceptable because content is separately scored by R1-SCOPE.

R3 requires documenting both collision_index and vehicle_reference relationships. The cited code-list fact explicitly supports collision_index as the join to Vehicle and Casualty, and the vehicle and casualty headers show a vehicle_reference column. However, no cited source fact explicitly states that vehicle_reference links casualty to vehicle, so the full R3 mapping is not fully evidenced.

R2-REQS overreaches by making the R8 summing/not-averaging rule part of R2 full credit, so the same property is scored under both R2 and R8. Its full-credit text also does not explicitly enumerate all required R2 variables, including collision_year, collision_injury_based, casualty_injury_based, vehicle_reference, and casualty_reference.

R3-MAP full credit requires documenting that vehicle_reference links casualty to vehicle, but the cited evidence only shows vehicle_reference as a column in the vehicle and casualty headers and explicitly supports collision_index as the join key. No cited source fact establishes the casualty-to-vehicle relationship, so the rubric tests an unsupported claim.
